We've always recommended that the public avoid sharing sensitive personal information when chatting with AI bots, since most companies use these conversations as training data. But now there's an even more serious reason to do so.

Last weekend, the situation took a dramatic turn when Reddit users discovered that the contents of some Claude AI conversations could be accessed through a simple Google search……

Claude Conversations Leaked

Claude has a sharing feature that allows users to share conversations with colleagues, friends, or family. The chat bot generates a link that users can send to one or more recipients, and Claude implicitly assures users that even those with the link cannot view the conversation content.

The problem is that Reddit users found that in reality, the conversations could be viewed without even obtaining the link. Users simply needed to search on Google—either using specific keywords or directly instructing Google to display all conversations shared in this manner—and everything would be laid bare. As reported by BBC News:

In practice, you just need to ask Google to search the directory Claude uses for sharing conversations (site:claude.ai/share), and you can access all the content.

As everyone might expect, some of the conversations were absurd—for example, someone asking why the music industry has been hiding the fact that most of Jay-Z's albums were actually co-written by birds. But others contained extremely sensitive information, including verbatim transcripts of private conversations; a lawyer inquiring whether they needed to proactively report a professional misconduct violation; and a user who inadvertently exposed their seed phrase while seeking help setting up a cryptocurrency wallet.

Anthropic is still trying to insist to this day that this is not a problem.

In fact, this is clearly an extremely serious issue, because it falls entirely outside the realm of what users could reasonably expect. What's worse, according to Wired magazine, the root cause appears to be extreme incompetence.

This incident comes on the heels of yesterday's report that Claude Cowork was able to escape the sandbox environment on Mac and gain full access to all files.

How to Protect Yourself

The problem appears to have been partially addressed, as previously accessible search results no longer display. However, given that the sharing feature relies on a 'security through obscurity' design principle, I recommend avoiding its use.

I also recommend deleting all previously shared conversations. Here's how: Go to Settings > Privacy > Shared Conversations > Manage.

Further Proof That Apple's Approach Is Superior

Apple Intelligence and the all-new Siri employ a three-tier privacy protection architecture:

  • Where feasible, AI processing is performed directly on the device
  • The first fallback is to use Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers
  • The final fallback is to use a Gemini model with protection levels equivalent to PCC

The highly sophisticated PCC architecture ensures that neither Apple nor Google can access any data, nor is any data retained. The security architecture designed by Apple allows for verification by independent security researchers.
